## What is Mounjaro?

Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is a once-weekly, injectable medication used for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes treatment. It’s the first dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, designed to improve insulin sensitivity, regulate blood sugar, reduce appetite, and promote sustained weight loss.

Mounjaro works by mimicking two natural gut hormones—glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). These hormones help regulate insulin levels, delay gastric emptying, and reduce cravings, resulting in a multi-faceted approach to metabolic support and appetite control. The dual-action mechanism makes Mounjaro more effective for many patients than GLP-1 therapies alone.

Initially developed for type 2 diabetes, Mounjaro has gained widespread clinical use for weight loss in non-diabetic individuals, especially those with obesity, insulin resistance, or metabolic syndrome. It’s FDA-approved for both indications and is commonly prescribed as part of a provider-managed weight loss program.

Administered via a simple, once-weekly subcutaneous injection, Mounjaro is a powerful tool for individuals looking to improve blood sugar control and achieve meaningful, sustainable weight loss—with provider oversight and long-term health in mind.

## Frequently Asked   Questions

Get answers to common questions about Mounjaro—how it works, what results to expect, and how to get started with dual-action GLP-1 and GIP therapy.

Want to explore more questions? [Read our full FAQ here](https://biltrx.com/frequently-asked-questions/)

How does Mounjaro work?

Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is a dual-acting GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist. It helps regulate blood sugar, slows digestion, suppresses appetite, and promotes weight loss by targeting two key incretin pathways instead of just one.

How is Mounjaro different from Semaglutide?

While both are GLP-1 receptor agonists, Mounjaro also activates the GIP receptor. This dual action may offer greater weight loss and blood sugar control benefits compared to GLP-1 medications alone.

How is Mounjaro administered?

Mounjaro is given as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Your provider will determine the right dosage and show you how to administer it at home.

How long does it take to see results?

Patients often notice reduced appetite within the first few weeks. More significant weight reduction and metabolic improvements are typically seen after 8–12 weeks of consistent use, especially when combined with diet and exercise.

What are the side effects of Mounjaro?

Common side effects include nausea, constipation, diarrhea, and decreased appetite. These are generally mild and improve over time. Rare but serious risks include pancreatitis and gallbladder issues.

## What is Ozempic?

Ozempic (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist used to treat type 2 diabetes and support chronic weight management. It mimics the GLP-1 hormone, which helps regulate blood sugar, reduce appetite, and slow digestion, leading to better glycemic control and gradual, sustained fat loss.

While originally developed for diabetes, Ozempic has become a widely used off-label solution for non-diabetic weight loss, particularly in individuals with obesity, insulin resistance, or metabolic syndrome. It works by stimulating insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, and decreasing hunger signals in the brain.

Ozempic is typically prescribed as part of a provider-monitored treatment plan that includes nutrition, movement, and behavior changes. It’s administered once weekly via subcutaneous injection and delivers clinically backed results in both metabolic health and weight reduction.

## Frequently Asked   Questions

Get answers to common questions about Ozempic—how it works, what results to expect, and how to begin treatment for type 2 diabetes management and overall health.

Want to explore more questions? [Read our full FAQ here](https://biltrx.com/frequently-asked-questions/)

What is Ozempic used for?

Ozempic (semaglutide) is FDA-approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. It helps regulate blood sugar levels and reduce the risk of cardiovascular events. While not specifically approved for weight loss, many patients also experience significant weight reduction as a secondary benefit.

How does Ozempic work?

Ozempic is a GLP-1 receptor agonist. It mimics the effects of a natural hormone that helps control blood sugar, slows digestion, reduces appetite, and promotes a feeling of fullness.

How is Ozempic administered?

Ozempic is a once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Your provider will guide you on proper injection technique and determine the appropriate dose based on your treatment plan.

How soon will I see results?

For type 2 diabetes, improvements in blood sugar may be noticeable within weeks. Weight-related benefits often appear after 2–3 months of consistent use.

What are the side effects of Ozempic?

The most common side effects include nausea, constipation, diarrhea, and decreased appetite. These generally improve over time. Serious but rare risks include pancreatitis and gallbladder issues.

By acting on areas of the brain involved in hunger and satiety, Wegovy helps reduce cravings, slow gastric emptying, and promote a feeling of fullness—leading to significant, sustainable weight loss. Administered subcutaneously, Wegovy is part of a provider-managed plan that ensures safe, consistent progress toward your weight loss goals—without the complexity of daily medications or invasive procedures.

How does Wegovy work?

Wegovy contains semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist that helps regulate appetite and food intake. It slows digestion, increases feelings of fullness, and reduces cravings, making it easier to lose weight.

How is Wegovy administered?

Wegovy is a once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Your provider will guide you on proper administration and dosing.

How soon will I see results with Wegovy?

Many patients notice decreased appetite within the first few weeks. More significant weight loss is typically seen after 2–3 months of consistent use, especially when combined with lifestyle changes.

What are the side effects of Wegovy?

Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and fatigue. These effects are usually mild and improve as your body adjusts. Serious but rare side effects include pancreatitis and gallbladder issues.

Who is Wegovy for?

Wegovy is FDA-approved for adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or those who are overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least one weight-related condition, such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, or high cholesterol.

## What is Zepbound?

Zepbound (tirzepatide) is an FDA-approved, once-weekly injectable medication used for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight and related medical conditions. It is the first and only dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist approved specifically for weight loss.

Zepbound works by mimicking two gut hormones—glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)—to reduce appetite, regulate blood sugar, improve insulin sensitivity, and support long-term fat loss. Its dual-action mechanism offers enhanced results compared to GLP-1 therapies alone.

Administered once weekly via subcutaneous injection, Zepbound is designed to be part of a comprehensive weight loss plan that includes provider care, lifestyle adjustments, and long-term monitoring. It’s ideal for individuals with insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, or significant weight loss goals.

What is Zepbound used for?

Zepbound (tirzepatide) is FDA-approved for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or those who are overweight with at least one weight-related condition.

How does Zepbound work?

Zepbound is a dual GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist. By activating two incretin pathways, it helps reduce appetite, slow digestion, regulate blood sugar, and promote meaningful weight loss.

How is Zepbound administered?

Zepbound is taken as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Your provider will guide you on proper injection technique and adjust your dosage as needed.

How quickly will I see results with Zepbound?

Many patients notice reduced hunger within the first few weeks. Clinically significant weight loss usually becomes more noticeable after 2–3 months of consistent treatment.

What are the side effects of Zepbound?

The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, constipation, and decreased appetite. These are usually temporary and improve over time. Rare but serious risks include pancreatitis or gallbladder issues.

## Everything you need to know about     Mounjaro®

[Basics](https://joinfound.com/medication/mounjaro#what-is) [Benefits](https://joinfound.com/medication/mounjaro#benefits) [How it works](https://joinfound.com/medication/mounjaro#how-it-works) [How to use it](https://joinfound.com/medication/mounjaro#how-to-use-it)

### What     is     are     Mounjaro®    ?

Mounjaro is a dual receptor agonist drug approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat Type 2 diabetes. Clinicians prescribe it off-label for weight loss because clinical evidence shows it also helps people lose weight.

‍ [More on off-label prescribing](https://joinfound.com/blog/off-label-weight-loss-medication-for-weight-loss)

Mounjaro is a brand name for tirzepatide and it is manufactured by Eli Lilly.

Mounjaro is available as an injection. Currently, there’s no generic version of Mounjaro that’s been approved by the FDA.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/660ed409e83c4d309ededa7c_medication-overview.webp)

### Benefits of     Mounjaro®

Expected weight loss depends on the dosage. In a study funded by its manufacturer, Eli Lilly, participants taking 15 mg of tirzepatide lost an average of 48 pounds over 72 weeks, while those taking 5 mg of tirzepatide lost 34 pounds.

Mounjaro also improves heart health by improving heart health metrics like blood pressure, blood sugar levels, and cholesterol, and helping people lose excess weight. Multiple clinical trials funded by Eli Lilly show tirzepatide can reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death in adults with Type 2 diabetes and those with overweight or obesity.

It’s significant to note that some patients have reported reduced [cravings](https://joinfound.com/blog/constant-cravings) and “food noise” and increased quality of life while using Mounjaro.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/660ed42ed7b133fd056884e3_benefits-overview.webp)

### How     does     do     Mounjaro®    work?

When you eat, the food stimulates your gut to release [GLP-1](https://joinfound.com/blog/glp-1-weight-loss) and [GIP](https://joinfound.com/blog/how-each-glp-1-works-for-weight-loss). When blood sugar levels are high after a meal, GLP-1 helps the pancreas release the right amount of insulin and slows how quickly the food moves through the digestive system. It also decreases glucagon, a hormone that controls the amount of glucose (blood sugar) the liver makes. GIP stimulates insulin release to help regulate low blood sugar levels after eating.

In some people, the gut doesn't make enough of these hormones on its own, or the brain isn't sensitive to them.

Mounjaro is a combination of synthetic GIP and GLP-1, which acts as a dual receptor agonist (RA). A drug that works as an agonist activates the same cell receptors as the body’s natural hormones. So, Mounjaro works in the gut like the body’s natural GLP-1 and GIP. Because Mounjaro slows digestion, it helps curb hunger and signal fullness to the brain. It also prompts insulin release, maintaining blood sugar levels after a meal. As a result, some people with obesity and overweight have lost weight while taking it.

Because Mounjaro supports a process the body isn’t doing well on its own, it may require [long-term use](https://joinfound.com/blog/do-i-have-to-take-glp-1-long-term).

It’s important to note that Mounjaro doesn’t work for everyone. There are many biological reasons why people struggle to lose weight. Found’s clinicians, trained in obesity medicine, can help patients identify the root cause of their weight gain and personalize a prescription to target it.  All prescriptions are up to a medical provider’s discretion.

[More on personalized treatment with Found](https://joinfound.com/blog/best-weight-loss-drugs)

‍

### How to use it

Mounjaro is typically taken once a week. Follow your care provider’s instructions for using it.

Eli Lilly recommends injecting Mounjaro under the skin in your upper arm, upper thigh, or stomach. Store the prefilled Mounjaro pens in a refrigerator.

‍

#### Dosing

Dosing depends on your specific prescription and your care provider’s instructions. Please also read the pharmaceutical packaging.

#### Side effects

Commonly reported side effects of this medication include:

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Stomach pain
- Constipation
- Gastrointestinal issues
- Bloating

Other potential side effects:

- Indigestion
- Dizziness
- Back pain
- Increased lipase or amylase
- Altered taste
- Nasopharyngitis (common cold)
- Passing gas
- Bloating
- Belching
- Gastroenteritis
- Decreased appetite
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease
- Upset stomach

These symptoms often subside as your body adjusts to the medications. Please notify your provider if side effects persist. **For a complete list of side effects, review the medication packaging inserts.**

[More on Mounjaro side effects](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/mounjaro-side-effects)

#### Black Box Warning

Although rare, Mounjaro caused thyroid C-cell tumors in animal studies. Mounjaro has a “black box” warning of the risk of these tumors. If you have trouble swallowing, develop hoarseness, or feel swelling or a lump in your neck, contact your health care provider immediately.

The FDA also warns not to take Zepbound if you have a personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome Type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer.

#### Precautions

Rapid or significant weight loss can lead to too much [muscle loss.](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/do-glp-1s-cause-muscle-loss) To protect your muscles, it’s important to start a strength training program and exercise regularly while taking Mounjaro.

Tell your health care provider if you have severe stomach problems that won’t go away, including abdominal bloating or pain, acid reflux, a feeling of fullness after eating just a few bites of food, nausea, and vomiting, including vomiting undigested food eaten a few hours earlier. These may be symptoms of gastroparesis (stomach paralysis).

Use effective contraception while taking this medication. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, do not take Mounjaro.

If you are going under general anesthesia or deep sedation, this medicine may make you accidentally breathe food or liquid into your lungs (pulmonary aspiration). Tell the providers who are performing the procedure that you take Mounjaro several weeks before the procedure, and follow their instructions.

Although rare, Mounjaro caused thyroid C-cell tumors in animal studies. Mounjaro has a “black box” warning of the risk of these tumors. If you have trouble swallowing, develop hoarseness, or feel swelling or a lump in your neck, contact your health care provider immediately.

The FDA also warns not to take Mounjaro if you have a personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome Type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer. Mounjaro is not appropriate for those with insulin-dependent diabetes. So, if that’s you, Mounjaro isn’t the right fit.

‍

#### Interactions

Some drugs can also interact with Mounjaro, including:

- Insulin
- Sulfonylureas (these can cause blood sugar levels to drop dangerously low)
- Some birth control pills
- Other GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist medications such as liraglutide, dulaglutide, or semaglutide

You should not drink alcohol while taking this drug because drinking can lower blood sugar. Combining alcohol with Mounjaro may cause blood sugar levels to fall too fast, leading to fainting and dizziness.

## Everything you need to know about     Ozempic®

[Basics](https://joinfound.com/medication/ozempic#what-is) [Benefits](https://joinfound.com/medication/ozempic#benefits) [How it works](https://joinfound.com/medication/ozempic#how-it-works) [How to use it](https://joinfound.com/medication/ozempic#how-to-use-it)

### What     is     are     Ozempic®    ?

Ozempic is a drug that is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat Type 2 diabetes and to reduce major heart events in adults who have Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Clinicians prescribe it off-label for weight loss because clinical evidence shows it also helps people lose weight.

[More on off-label prescribing](https://joinfound.com/blog/off-label-weight-loss-medication-for-weight-loss)

Ozempic is a brand name for semaglutide which Novo Nordisk manufactures. It is a synthetic version of the GLP-1 hormone.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/69d025f0609ed0a2cd821496_685c4f3b3fa462553ab74043_b2b-hero-bg-mobile.avif)

### Benefits of     Ozempic®

Expected weight loss depends on the dosage of Ozempic. In one study, people who took 2.4 mg of semaglutide every week for 68 weeks lost an average of 14.9% of their total body weight. (Safe weight loss is one to two pounds per week.)

Although Ozempic is a diabetes medication, it may have more benefits for off-label use beyond weight management. Multiple clinical trials funded by Novo Nordisk show semaglutide can reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death in adults with Type 2 diabetes and known heart disease.

Semaglutide improves heart health by lowering blood sugar and helping people lose excess body weight. Research is ongoing to determine if semaglutide can treat other medical conditions.

And it’s significant to note that some patients have reported reduced cravings while using semaglutide for weight loss.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/660ed42ed7b133fd056884e3_benefits-overview.webp)

### How     does     do     Ozempic®    work?

When you eat, your food stimulates your gut to release the [GLP-1 hormone](https://joinfound.com/blog/glp-1-weight-loss). GLP-1 helps lower blood glucose (blood sugar) by stimulating insulin release. And insulin helps blood glucose enter your body’s cells for later energy use.

In some people, the gut doesn't make enough natural GLP-1, or the brain isn't sensitive to it.

[‍](https://joinfound.com/) Ozempic is a synthetic GLP-1 RA or glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist. A drug that works as an agonist activates the same cell receptors as the body's natural hormones. So, Ozempic works in the gut like natural GLP-1. Because Ozempic slows digestion, it helps curb hunger and signal fullness to the brain. As a result, some people with obesity have lost weight while taking it.

Because Ozempic supports a process the body isn’t doing well, it’s intended for [long-term use](https://joinfound.com/blog/do-i-have-to-take-glp-1-long-term).

It’s important to note that GLP-1 medications don’t work for everyone. There are dozens of biological reasons why people struggle to lose weight. Found’s health care providers, trained in obesity medicine, can help patients identify the root cause of their weight gain and personalize a prescription to target it.

[More on personalized treatment with Found](https://joinfound.com/blog/best-weight-loss-drugs)

### How to use it

Physicians typically instruct patients to take Ozempic once a week. Novo Nordisk recommends injecting the medicine under the skin in your upper arm, upper thigh, or stomach. Store Ozempic in a refrigerator.

#### Dosing

For most patients, dosing begins with the 0.25 mg pen for weekly injections for the first four weeks and increases to 0.5 mg on the fifth week of treatment. After that, your provider may increase your weekly dose to 1 mg, then 2 mg as clinically needed for additional glycemic control for those with Type 2 diabetes and if you continue to tolerate semaglutide injections.

‍

#### Side effects

#### Common side effects

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Headache
- Fatigue
- Injection site reactions

Other potential side effects:

- Indigestion
- Dizziness
- Back pain
- Increased lipase or amylase
- Altered taste
- Nasopharyngitis (common cold)
- Passing gas
- Bloating
- Belching
- Gastroenteritis
- Decreased appetite
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease
- Upset stomach

These symptoms often subside as your body adjusts to the medications. Please notify your provider if side effects persist. **For a complete list of side effects, review the medication packaging inserts.**

‍

#### Black Box Warning

Although rare, semaglutide caused thyroid C-cell tumors in animal studies. Ozempic’s “black box” warns of the risk of these tumors. If you have trouble swallowing, develop hoarseness, or feel swelling or a lump in your neck, contact your health care provider immediately.

The FDA also warns not to take Ozempic if you have or have a family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome Type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer.

#### Precautions

Rapid or significant weight loss can lead to too much [muscle loss](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/do-glp-1s-cause-muscle-loss). It’s important to start a strength training program and exercise regularly to protect your muscles while taking Ozempic.

Use adequate contraception while taking this medication. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, do not take Ozempic.

Tell your health care provider if you have severe stomach problems that won’t go away, including abdominal bloating or pain, acid reflux, a feeling of fullness after eating just a few bites of food, nausea, and vomiting, including vomiting undigested food eaten a few hours earlier. These may be symptoms of gastroparesis (stomach paralysis).

Severe pain in your abdomen or back that will not go away is a symptom of pancreatitis. Contact your health care provider immediately.

Ozempic is not appropriate for those with insulin-dependent diabetes. So, if that’s you, Ozempic isn’t the right fit.

#### Interactions

Some drugs can also interact with Ozempic, including:

- Insulin
- Sulfonylureas (when combined, these can cause blood sugar levels to drop dangerously low when combined with Ozempic)
- Some birth control pills
- Other GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist medications such as liraglutide, dulaglutide, or tirzepatide

You should not drink alcohol while taking these drugs because it can lower blood sugar. Combining alcohol with these medications may cause blood sugars to fall too fast, leading to fainting and dizziness.

## Alternative medications

Depending on your health history, weight history, and [MetabolicPrintTM assessment](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/best-weight-loss-drugs), your Found health care provider may consider other alternatives to help you lose weight. Some are FDA-approved for weight loss. Others are used off-label and have strong clinical evidence supporting their use for weight loss.

Unfortunately, there are no generic versions of Ozempic currently on the market.

However, your health care provider might consider alternatives such as Wegovy, Mounjaro, or Saxenda, all of which are GLP-1 medications but not all are FDA-approved for weight loss specifically.

## Everything you need to know about     Wegovy®

[Basics](https://joinfound.com/medication/wegovy#what-is) [Benefits](https://joinfound.com/medication/wegovy#benefits) [How it works](https://joinfound.com/medication/wegovy#how-it-works) [How to use it](https://joinfound.com/medication/wegovy#how-to-use-it)

### What     is     are     Wegovy®    ?

Wegovy is a drug approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat obesity and those with excess weight who have at least one weight-related medical issue.

Wegovy is a brand name for an injectable [semaglutide](https://joinfound.com/blog/wegovy-vs-ozempic) manufactured by Novo Nordisk. It is a synthetic version of the GLP-1 hormone. There is no generic version approved by the FDA.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/69d025e0bf807c5081fd4198_685c4f3c4237bf5c104d6b81_b2b-tour-03.avif)

### Benefits of     Wegovy®

Expected weight loss depends on the dosage of Wegovy and your lifestyle. In one large clinical trial, patients on 2.4 mg of Wegovy each week who received individualized lifestyle counseling sessions, followed a low-calorie diet, and increased physical activity lost an average of almost 15% of their body weight after 68 weeks. (Safe weight loss is one to two pounds per week.)

Wegovy also has more benefits than treating obesity and weight-related medical problems. In March 2024, the FDA approved Wegovy to prevent major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in people who have a history of heart disease. In clinical trials funded by Novo Nordisk, researchers found Wegovy reduces the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death in adults with obesity or overweight who also have cardiovascular disease. Semaglutide improves heart health by lowering blood sugar and helping people lose excess weight.

And it’s significant to note that some patients have reported reduced cravings while using semaglutide for weight loss.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/660ed42ed7b133fd056884e3_benefits-overview.webp)

### How     does     do     Wegovy®    work?

Eating triggers the release of [GLP-1](https://joinfound.com/blog/glp-1-weight-loss) in the gut. This hormone helps lower blood glucose (blood sugar) by stimulating insulin secretion, and insulin helps blood glucose enter your body’s cells for later energy use.

In some people, the gut doesn't make enough natural GLP-1, or the brain isn't sensitive to it.

Wegovy is a synthetic GLP-1 receptor agonist (RA). Agonists activate the same cell receptors as the body's natural chemical messengers. So, Wegovy works in the body like its natural GLP-1. Because Wegovy slows digestion, it helps curb hunger and signal fullness to the brain. As a result, some people with obesity have lost weight while taking it.

Because Wegovy supports a process the body isn’t doing well, it may require long-term use.

It’s important to note that GLP-1 medications don’t work for everyone. There are dozens of biological reasons why people struggle to lose weight. Found’s clinicians, trained in obesity medicine, can help patients identify the [root cause](https://joinfound.com/blog/best-weight-loss-drugs) of their weight gain and personalize a prescription to target it. All prescriptions are up to a medical provider’s discretion.

[More on personalized treatment with Found](https://joinfound.com/blog/best-weight-loss-drugs)

‍

### How to use it

Take Wegovy as instructed by a qualified health care provider. Novo Nordisk recommends injecting the medicine once a week under the skin in the upper arm, upper thigh, or stomach. Store the single-dose Wegovy pens in the refrigerator.

#### Dosing

For most patients, dosing typically begins with the 0.25 mg pen for weekly injections for the first four weeks. The dose increases to 0.5 mg on the fifth week of treatment. After that, your provider may increase your weekly dose, every four weeks, to 1 mg, then 1.7 mg, and highest 2.4 mg, as clinically needed for weight loss and if you continue to tolerate Wegovy injections.

#### Side effects

Commonly reported side effects of this medication include:

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Stomach pain
- Constipation
- Gastrointestinal issues
- Bloating

Other potential side effects:

- Indigestion
- Dizziness
- Back pain
- Increased lipase or amylase
- Altered taste
- Nasopharyngitis (common cold)
- Passing gas
- Bloating
- Belching
- Gastroenteritis
- Decreased appetite
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease
- Upset stomach

These symptoms often subside as your body adjusts to the medications. Please notify your provider if side effects persist. **For a complete list of side effects, review the medication packaging inserts.**

#### Black Box Warning

Although rare, semaglutide caused thyroid C-cell tumors in animal studies. Wegovy’s “black box” warns of the risk of these tumors. If you have trouble swallowing, develop hoarseness, or feel swelling or a lump in your neck, contact your health care provider immediately.

The FDA also warns not to take Wegovy if you have a personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome Type 2, or medullary thyroid cancer.

#### Precautions

Rapid or significant weight loss can lead to too much [muscle loss](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/do-glp-1s-cause-muscle-loss). It’s important to start a strength training program and exercise regularly to protect your muscles while taking Wegovy.

Tell your health care provider if you have severe stomach problems that won’t go away, including abdominal bloating or pain, acid reflux, a feeling of fullness after eating just a few bites of food, nausea, and vomiting, including vomiting undigested food eaten a few hours earlier. These may be symptoms of gastroparesis (stomach paralysis).

Use effective contraception while taking this medication. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, do not take Wegovy.

Wegovy isn’t appropriate for people who have insulin-dependent diabetes. So, if that’s you, Wegovy isn’t the right fit.

If you are going under general anesthesia or deep sedation, GLP-1s may make you accidentally breathe food or liquid into your lungs (pulmonary aspiration). Tell the providers who are performing your procedure that you take Wegovy several weeks before the procedure, and follow their instructions.

#### Interactions

Some drugs can also interact with Wegovy, including:

- Insulin
- Sulfonylureas (these can cause blood sugar levels to drop dangerously low when combined with Wegovy)
- Some birth control pills
- Other GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist medications such as liraglutide, dulaglutide, or tirzepatide

You should not drink alcohol while taking this drug because alcohol can lower blood sugar. Combining alcohol with Wegovy may cause blood sugars to fall too fast, leading to fainting and dizziness.

## Alternative medications

Depending on your health history, weight history, and [MetabolicPrintTM assessment](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/best-weight-loss-drugs), your Found health care provider may consider other alternatives to help you lose weight. Some are FDA-approved for weight loss. Others are used off-label and have strong clinical evidence supporting their use for weight loss.

Unfortunately, there are no generic versions of Ozempic currently on the market.

However, your health care provider might consider alternatives such as Wegovy, Mounjaro, or Saxenda, all of which are GLP-1 medications but not all are FDA-approved for weight loss specifically.

## Everything you need to know about     Zepbound®

[Basics](https://joinfound.com/medication/zepbound#what-is) [Benefits](https://joinfound.com/medication/zepbound#benefits) [How it works](https://joinfound.com/medication/zepbound#how-it-works) [How to use it](https://joinfound.com/medication/zepbound#how-to-use-it)

### What     is     are     Zepbound®    ?

Zepbound is a drug approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for chronic weight management. It mimics the [GLP-1 and GIP hormones](https://joinfound.com/blog/glp-vs-glp-1) and is prescribed to treat obesity or overweight (a body mass index of 27+ with at least one weight-related health condition). Zepbound is a brand name for [tirzepatide](https://joinfound.com/blog/tirzepatide-weight-loss), which is manufactured by Eli Lilly.

Zepbound is available as an injection. Currently, the FDA has not approved a generic version of Zepbound.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/69d025f0609ed0a2cd821496_685c4f3b3fa462553ab74043_b2b-hero-bg-mobile.avif)

### Benefits of     Zepbound®

Expected weight loss depends on the dosage.

In a study funded by its manufacturer, Eli Lilly, participants taking 15 mg of tirzepatide lost an average of 48 pounds over 72 weeks, while those taking 5 mg of tirzepatide lost 34 pounds.

Zepbound also improves heart health by improving heart health metrics like blood pressure, blood sugar levels, and cholesterol, and helping people lose excess weight. Multiple clinical trials funded by Eli Lilly show Zepbound can reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke, or death in adults with Type 2 diabetes and those with overweight or obesity.

It’s significant to note that some patients have reported reduced [cravings](https://joinfound.com/blog/constant-cravings) and “food noise” and increased quality of life while using Zepbound.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/660dbd9edac735ff882da2d3/665a684534335a651fefd916_09_Hands_0846.webp)

### How     does     do     Zepbound®    work?

When you eat, the food stimulates your gut to release [GLP-1](https://joinfound.com/blog/glp-1-weight-loss) and [GIP](https://joinfound.com/blog/how-each-glp-1-works-for-weight-loss). When blood sugar levels are high after a meal, GLP-1 helps the pancreas release the right amount of insulin and slows how quickly the food moves through the digestive system. It also decreases glucagon, a hormone that controls the amount of glucose (blood sugar) the liver makes. GIP stimulates insulin release to help regulate blood sugar levels after eating.

In some people, the gut doesn't make enough of these hormones on its own, or the brain isn't sensitive to them.

Zepbound is a combination of synthetic GIP and GLP-1, which acts as a dual receptor agonist (RA).  A drug that works as an agonist activates the same cell receptors as the body’s natural hormones. So, Zepbound works in the gut like the body’s natural GLP-1 and GIP. Because Zepbound slows digestion, it helps curb hunger and signal fullness to the brain. It also prompts insulin release, maintaining blood sugar levels after a meal. As a result, some people with obesity and excess weight have lost weight while taking it.

Because Zepbound supports a process the body isn’t doing well on its own, it may require [long-term use](https://joinfound.com/blog/do-i-have-to-take-glp-1-long-term).

It’s important to note that Zepbound doesn’t work for everyone. There are many biological reasons why people struggle to lose weight. Found’s clinicians, trained in obesity medicine, can help patients identify the root cause of their weight gain and personalize a prescription to target it.  All prescriptions are up to a medical provider’s discretion.

‍

[More on personalized treatment with Found](https://joinfound.com/blog/best-weight-loss-drugs)

### How to use it

Zepbound is typically taken once a week. Follow your care provider’s instructions for using it.

Eli Lilly recommends injecting Zepbound under the skin in your upper arm, upper thigh, or stomach. Store the prefilled Zepbound pens in a refrigerator.

#### Dosing

Dosing depends on your specific prescription and your care provider’s instructions. Please also read the pharmaceutical packaging.

#### Side effects

Commonly reported side effects of this medication include:

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Stomach pain
- Constipation
- Gastrointestinal issues
- Bloating

Other potential side effects:

- Indigestion
- Dizziness
- Back pain
- Increased lipase or amylase
- Altered taste
- Nasopharyngitis (common cold)
- Passing gas
- Bloating
- Belching
- Gastroenteritis
- Decreased appetite
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease
- Upset stomach

These symptoms often subside as your body adjusts to the medications. Please notify your provider if side effects persist. **For a complete list of side effects, review the medication packaging inserts.**

[More on Zepbound side effects](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/zepbound-side-effects)

#### Black Box Warning

Although rare, Zepbound caused thyroid C-cell tumors in animal studies. Zepbound has a “black box” warning of the risk of these tumors. If you have trouble swallowing, develop hoarseness, or feel swelling or a lump in your neck, contact your health care provider immediately.

The FDA also warns not to take Zepbound if you have a personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome Type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer.

#### Precautions

Rapid or significant weight loss can lead to too much [muscle loss.](https://joinfound.com/blogs/posts/do-glp-1s-cause-muscle-loss) To protect your muscles, it’s important to start a strength training program and exercise regularly while taking Zepbound.

Tell your health care provider if you have severe stomach problems that won’t go away, including abdominal bloating or pain, acid reflux, a feeling of fullness after eating just a few bites of food, nausea, and vomiting, including vomiting undigested food eaten a few hours earlier. These may be symptoms of gastroparesis (stomach paralysis).

Use effective contraception while taking this medication. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, do not take Zepbound.

If you are going under general anesthesia or deep sedation, this medicine may make you accidentally breathe food or liquid into your lungs (pulmonary aspiration).

Zepbound is not appropriate for those with insulin-dependent diabetes. So, if that’s you, Zepbound isn’t the right fit.

#### Interactions

Some drugs can also interact with Zepbound, including:

- Insulin
- Sulfonylureas (these can cause blood sugar levels to drop dangerously low)
- Some birth control pills
- Other GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist medications such as liraglutide, dulaglutide, or semaglutide

You should not drink alcohol while taking this drug because drinking can lower blood sugar. Combining alcohol with Zepbound may cause blood sugar levels to fall too fast, leading to fainting and dizziness.

## Frequently Asked Questions

See if you qualify

What are my weight loss treatment options through Gala GLP-1?▼

Gala GLP-1 offers access to a range of prescription options to support individuals with high BMI, obesity, or weight-related health concerns. These options include FDA-approved medications for weight management, as well as compounded medications prepared by licensed pharmacies in accordance with a provider’s prescription.

Your treatment plan will be personalized by a licensed healthcare provider based on your individual health profile and weight loss goals.

Please note: While some medications available through Gala GLP-1 are FDA-approved for weight management, compounded medications are not reviewed or approved by the FDA. They are prepared to meet the specific needs of individual patients when commercially available options are not suitable.


How much does weight loss treatment cost?▼

Through Gala GLP-1, you can access GLP-1 weight loss medications (not-FDA approved) starting at just $199 per month (with a 3-month plan). Final pricing is determined at checkout based on your selected plan and medication. We leverage our scale and partnerships to provide affordable access to high-quality compounded GLP-1s—ensuring you receive effective treatment without unnecessary costs.


Are video visits with a doctor required?▼

Depending on the patient, state laws, or type of medication, consultations may be synchronous—such as a video visit—or asynchronous, like online messaging. If a video visit is required, it will typically be for the initial session. After that, follow-ups, adjustments, and questions may be handled through the Gala GLP-1 chat.


Is insurance required?▼

No, Gala GLP-1 does not require insurance. We offer transparent pricing and straightforward
billing, ensuring you have access to affordable treatment without the complexities of insurance.
Our goal is to make your weight loss journey as simple and accessible as possible.


Which Pharmacies Do We Partner With?▼

We work with a wide network of pharmacies across all 50 states. This nationwide coverage ensures that patients can reliably access the medications they need (not-FDA approved), no matter their location.

Medical services are provided by licensed physicians and clinicians affiliated with independently owned and operated medical practices, including OpenLoop-affiliated medical groups and other affiliated medical practices. Gala provides administrative, technology, and management services and does not provide medical care.


How do I know if I qualify for treatment?▼

A state‑licensed healthcare provider will carefully review your health history, weight loss goals,
and individual needs to determine if GLP‑1 treatment is right for you. This evaluation ensures that
every prescription is safe and appropriate before you begin your weight loss journey.


Are GLP-1s available in all states?▼

Yes! Gala GLP-1 provides access to GLP-1 medications in all 50 states, ensuring that no matter
where you live, you can start your weight loss journey with our treatments.


How long do I need to stay on the medication?▼

GLP-1 medications (not-FDA approved) are designed for long-term use and are not intended as a short-term solution.
If treatment is stopped, the factors that previously contributed to weight gain may return.
It’s important to consult with your healthcare provider before making any changes to your medication plan.


When will I see weight loss results?▼

Weight loss takes time, and results won’t happen overnight. Every individual’s journey is unique,
so the timeline for noticeable changes varies. Consistency with treatment and lifestyle adjustments
will play a key role in your progress.


How are compounded GLP-1s sourced?▼

Our compounded GLP-1 medications are not FDA-approved but are made using ingredients sourced from FDA-regulated suppliers and are prepared following strict quality and safety protocols.


What are the potential side effects of GLP-1 medications?▼

As your body adapts to GLP-1 medications (not-FDA approved), you may experience temporary side effects such as nausea, upset stomach, or digestive discomfort. These symptoms are common and often improve over time. At Gala GLP-1, we support you every step of the way with:

✔ Personalized dosage adjustments—Your provider will tailor your dosage and adjust it as needed.
✔ Async messaging with a licensed provider—Get expert guidance anytime at no extra cost.
✔ Step-by-step support—Access expert-created guides to help manage side effects.



Can my provider adjust my dosage during treatment?▼

Yes! Your provider can modify your dosage at any time to align with your medical history, progress, and weight loss goals. If a higher dose is recommended, it will be available at no additional cost. Your treatment plan is personalized and flexible, ensuring you receive the right dosage for your needs throughout your journey.


Can I switch medication kits if my current medication isn’t working?▼

Yes! If your current medication isn’t delivering the expected results, your provider can adjust
your prescription at no additional cost. Your treatment is personalized to ensure you receive
the most effective option for your weight loss journey.


Are there side effects associated with GLP-1 medications?▼

Yes, like most prescription medications, GLP-1 treatments can cause side effects—often mild gastrointestinal issues such as nausea or diarrhea. We recommend discussing potential risks and benefits with your healthcare provider to determine if GLP-1 medication is right for you. If you experience severe or persistent side effects, contact your provider immediately.

## Important Safety Information

Read More

Your health and safety are our top priorities. This medication is not suitable for everyone. It is essential to provide a complete and accurate medical history during your online consultation for our physicians to determine if this treatment is appropriate for you.

Boxed Warning:

In animal studies, semaglutide caused thyroid tumors or thyroid cancer. It is not known if this may occur in people. You should not use this medication if you or any of your family have ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have an endocrine system condition called Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2). Call your doctor at once if you notice signs of a thyroid tumor, such as a lump or swelling in your neck, trouble swallowing, a hoarse voice, or shortness of breath.

Do NOT take Oral Semaglutide if you:

- Have a personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2.
- Have a known allergy to semaglutide or any of its ingredients.
- Have diabetic ketoacidosis.

Before taking this medication, tell your provider about all of your medical conditions, especially if you have or have had:

- A history of pancreatitis.
- Stomach, intestinal, or kidney problems.
- A history of diabetic retinopathy (eye problems).
- You are pregnant, breastfeeding, or plan to become pregnant.

What are the possible side effects?

The most common side effects are generally mild and temporary. They may include:

- Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation
- Stomach pain, bloating, heartburn, or gas
- Headache, dizziness, or tiredness

## Frequently Asked Questions

How much weight can I expect to lose?

Clinical trials show average weight loss of 15-20% of body weight over 68 weeks. Individual results vary based on adherence, diet, exercise, and starting weight. Most patients see noticeable results within 8-12 weeks.

What are the common side effects?

The most common side effects are gastrointestinal: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation. These typically improve as your body adjusts. Starting with a low dose and gradually increasing helps minimize side effects.

How long do I need to take semaglutide?

Semaglutide is typically used as long as weight management benefits continue. Discontinuing may result in weight regain. Your provider will work with you on a long-term plan.

Can I take semaglutide with other medications?

Semaglutide may interact with certain medications, especially those affecting blood sugar. Provide a complete medication list during intake so your provider can assess safety.

How do I take sublingual semaglutide?

Place the prescribed number of drops under your tongue and hold for 30-60 seconds before swallowing. Take on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating or drinking.

Will I have the same side effects as injectable?

Are the side effects stronger than semaglutide?

FAQ

### What is Wegovy®?

Wegovy® (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved prescription medication used for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or excess weight. It belongs to a class of medications called GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Wegovy® works by mimicking a natural hormone in your body that helps regulate appetite and blood sugar, which can support reduced food intake and healthier eating patterns when combined with lifestyle changes.

FAQ

### How effective is Wegovy® for weight loss?

Wegovy® has been clinically studied for weight management. In clinical trials, adults who used Wegovy® alongside diet and lifestyle changes lost an average of 14–15% of their body weight over one year.\*

Individual results vary based on factors such as dosage, adherence, lifestyle habits, and overall health.

FAQ

### What is the Wegovy® pill, and how is it different from the Wegovy® pen?

Both the Wegovy® pill and the Wegovy® pen contain the same active ingredient, semaglutide, and are FDA-approved for weight management. The main difference is how and how often they’re taken.

Similarities:

- Both are FDA-approved Wegovy® formulations
- Both use semaglutide as the active ingredient
- Both follow a gradual dose-increase schedule determined by a provider
- Side effects are generally similar and can be managed with provider support

Differences:

- Wegovy® pen: Taken as a once-weekly injection
- Wegovy® pill: Taken orally once per day

Your Shed provider will help determine which option may be appropriate based on your health history, preferences, and treatment goals.

FAQ

### What’s the difference between Ozempic® and Wegovy®?

Both medications contain semaglutide, but they are FDA-approved for different uses.

- Ozempic® is approved to treat type 2 diabetes
- Wegovy® is specifically approved for chronic weight management

In some cases, providers may prescribe Ozempic® off-label for weight management when appropriate, but Wegovy® is the formulation designed and approved for weight loss.

## Questions? We’ve got answers.

Health

### What is Wegovy®?

Wegovy® (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved prescription medication used for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or excess weight. It belongs to a class of medications called GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Wegovy® works by mimicking a natural hormone in your body that helps regulate appetite and blood sugar, which can support reduced food intake and healthier eating patterns when combined with lifestyle changes.

‍

Health

### How effective is Wegovy® for weight loss?

Wegovy® has been clinically studied for weight management. In clinical trials, adults who used Wegovy® alongside diet and lifestyle changes lost an average of 14–15% of their body weight over one year.\*

Individual results vary based on factors such as dosage, adherence, lifestyle habits, and overall health.

Health

### What is the Wegovy® pill, and how is it different from the Wegovy® pen?

Both the Wegovy® pill and the Wegovy® pen contain the same active ingredient, semaglutide, and are FDA-approved for weight management. The main difference is how and how often they’re taken.Similarities:

- Both are FDA-approved Wegovy® formulations
- Both use semaglutide as the active ingredient
- Both follow a gradual dose-increase schedule determined by a provider
- Side effects are generally similar and can be managed with provider support

Differences:

- Wegovy® pen: Taken as a once-weekly injection
- Wegovy® pill: Taken orally once per day

Your Shed provider will help determine which option may be appropriate based on your health history, preferences, and treatment goals.

Health

### What’s the difference between Ozempic® and Wegovy®?

Both medications contain semaglutide, but they are FDA-approved for different uses.

- Ozempic® is approved to treat type 2 diabetes
- Wegovy® is specifically approved for chronic weight management

In some cases, providers may prescribe Ozempic® off-label for weight management when appropriate, but Wegovy® is the formulation designed and approved for weight loss.

Health

### How does Shed’s Wegovy® program work?

Shed provides access to Wegovy® through a fully online, provider-led care model.

If prescribed, your program includes:

- A medical review by a licensed provider
- Ongoing provider support and follow-ups
- Text-based Health Coaching\*\*
- Educational tools and resources
- A supportive community to help you stay on track

Medication costs are separate from the monthly Shed membership.

Health

### Is Wegovy® right for everyone?

Wegovy® is not appropriate for everyone. A licensed healthcare provider will review your health history and goals to determine whether Wegovy® may be a safe and suitable option for you.

[See more in our help center](https://www.tryshed.com/resources/help-dep)

_Compounded medications are prepared by licensed pharmacies to meet the specific needs of individual patients. These medications are not reviewed or approved by the FDA for safety, effectiveness, or quality. However, they are made in accordance with strict regulatory guidelines. If your clinician determines that a compounded medication is clinically appropriate for you, please be aware that it is not an FDA-approved product._

_Ozempic®, Wegovy®, and Rybelsus® are the only FDA-approved products containing semaglutide produced by Novo Nordisk, Inc., while Zepbound® and Mounjaro® are the only FDA-approved products containing tirzepatide produced by Lilly USA LLC._

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is Semaglutide?

Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist. It mimics a hormone your body makes naturally to help regulate appetite and blood sugar.\*

How does Semaglutide work?

Semaglutide signals the brain regarding satiety, slows how quickly food leaves the stomach, and supports insulin sensitivity. This may result in reduced hunger and smaller portions when paired with healthy lifestyle changes.\*

What are the benefits of Semaglutide for weight management?

Semaglutide may help reduce appetite and cravings, support more stable blood sugar, and lead to sustainable weight management when combined with nutrition and activity changes, all under physician supervision.\*

How is Semaglutide taken?

The compounded injectable is a once-weekly subcutaneous injection, typically into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. The oral option is a buccal lozenge placed between the cheek and gum and allowed to dissolve as directed by your doctor. Your physician will guide you through dose titration over the first weeks either way.

What is the difference between injectable and oral Semaglutide?

Both formats contain Semaglutide. The injectable is a once-weekly shot, while the oral lozenge is a daily dose that dissolves between the cheek and gum, no needles required. Your provider can help you choose based on your preference and treatment plan.

What results can I expect with Semaglutide?

Results vary by individual and depend on your starting point, dose, and lifestyle habits. Your provider will adjust your plan based on how you respond.\*

How long until I see results?

Many patients notice changes in appetite within the first few weeks, with progress occurring over a 3 to 12 month plan when paired with healthy nutrition and movement.\*

How long do I need to stay on Semaglutide?

Treatment length is personalized with your physician and depends on your goals. Many patients continue on a maintenance dose to help sustain results after their initial phase.

## How semaglutide works

GLP-1 receptor agonism, the original mechanism that defined modern metabolic therapy.

### GLP-1 receptor activation

Binds and activates GLP-1 receptors in the pancreas, brain, and gut, mimicking the incretin signal your body already uses to regulate glucose and appetite.

### Appetite & satiety regulation

Slows gastric emptying and signals fullness in the hypothalamus, shifting your set-point for hunger and meal size.

### Glucose stabilisation

Stimulates insulin release when glucose is high and suppresses glucagon, flattening post-meal spikes over weeks.

Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 alone; tirzepatide acts on both GLP-1 and GIP. Tirzepatide produces more weight loss in head-to-head trials, but semaglutide has the longest clinical track record and is often the right starting point.

Most patients notice appetite changes in the first 1–2 weeks and meaningful weight changes by week 6–8. Full results accrue over 6–12 months as the dose is titrated.

## Frequently asked questions

Everything you need to know about Oral GLP-1.

Is oral GLP-1 as effective as the injectable?

It uses the same molecules. Bioavailability through sublingual delivery is lower than subcutaneous injection, so dose strength is adjusted accordingly. Your clinician matches your protocol to your goals during intake. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved and individual results vary.

How do I take it?

One daily dose held under your tongue for 60–90 seconds, then swallowed. Take it at the same time each day for consistent exposure, most patients do it with morning coffee or before bed.

Why daily instead of weekly?

Sublingual delivery clears the system faster than the weekly subcutaneous depot. Daily dosing maintains steadier blood levels and tends to produce smoother appetite control.

GI side effects are typically milder than the injectable because peak blood levels are lower, and the tirzepatide formulation is prepared with ondansetron, an anti-nausea medication, to help manage nausea. Some patients notice a mild tingling under the tongue during the first few doses.

FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

Everything you need to know about Tirzepatide.

Is Tirzepatide right for me?

Tirzepatide is most often considered for adults with a BMI of 27+ (with at least one weight-related condition) or 30+. If your BMI is lower, microdosed tirzepatide is available to those with a BMI of 19 and above, for metabolic optimization and steady body recomposition rather than aggressive weight loss. Your US-licensed clinician reviews your intake and labs to confirm the right fit before prescribing.

How quickly will I see results?

That varies from person to person, and we cannot promise a timeline or a result. Your provider sets your starting dose and adjusts it based on how you respond. Compounded tirzepatide is not FDA-approved, and individual results vary and are not guaranteed.

What about side effects?

The most common side effects are GI-related (nausea, mild reflux, transient constipation) and typically settle as your dose is titrated. Your care team adjusts your dose based on tolerance. You can also add B12 to your GLP-1 protocol to help minimize nausea, your clinician can include it when it's a good fit for you.

How is this different from Semaglutide?

Tirzepatide is a dual GLP-1 + GIP agonist, semaglutide acts on GLP-1 alone. Head-to-head trials show greater weight loss with tirzepatide, with a similar safety profile.

What's included in my subscription?

Your medication shipped from a licensed US compound pharmacy, free 2-day shipping, unlimited messaging with your care team, dose adjustments as your body changes, and quarterly labs.

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes, one click in your portal, no retention call, no penalties. You only pay for the cycle you're in.

Which pharmacy dispenses my medication?

Your prescriptions are fulfilled by our partner compounding pharmacy, VialsRX, an AI-powered pharmacy specializing in personalized compounding for weight management and anti-aging treatments. They can be contacted at: 6220 Westpark Dr, Houston, TX 77057 · (713) 497-5590 · [vials.ai](https://vials.ai/).

We also partner with F&F Pharmacies Inc dba Jungle Jim’s Pharmacy, located at 5484 Dixie Highway, Fairfield, OH 45014. They can be contacted at [(877) 858-3784](tel:+18778583784). They are able to dispense medications and maintain a license in 40 US states. Unfortunately, they cannot dispense sterile compounds and do not have a license in the following US states: California, Nevada, New Jersey, North Carolina, Texas, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Hampshire, West Virginia, and Delaware.

Are these services available in my state?

Yes. Services are available in all 50 US states through our affiliated medical providers and pharmacy partners. All operations strictly adhere to applicable state licensure requirements.

Why does medication selection vary by location?

Certain medications, specific formulations, or fulfillment options may vary. This is due to state-specific pharmacy regulations and local dispensing restrictions that our partners must follow.

How can I contact the medical provider?

You can reach their compliance and medical team directly via email at [medicalcompliance@arorahealthgroup.com](mailto:medicalcompliance@arorahealthgroup.com). Their administrative office is located at 300 Lenora Street, Seattle, WA 98121. You can also visit their website at [arora-health.com](https://arora-health.com/).

Who are our clinical providers?

### FREQUENTLY   ASKED QUESTIONS:

#### [VIEW ALL FAQS >](https://trtnation.com/faqs/)

#### [Who qualifies for weight loss medications?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672779131702-9f75dc10-f756)

Eligibility is determined by a healthcare provider and isn’t guaranteed. Typically, candidates include Adults 25+ with a BMI over 25.

#### [What makes medical weight loss different from dieting on my own?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1775831959561-67b78d29-36c0)

Diet and exercise alone work for some people, but for many, hormonal resistance, metabolic dysfunction, and hunger signaling make sustainable weight loss extremely difficult. Medical weight loss uses prescribed and clinically proven medications to work with your biology — not against it — so you can finally see results that last.

#### [What is tirzepatide and how does it work?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1775832029021-e690f52f-19e0)

Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, meaning it activates two separate hormonal pathways that regulate blood sugar, appetite, and fat storage. It slows gastric emptying, reduces appetite dramatically, and helps your body use energy more efficiently. Clinical trials have shown average weight loss of 15–20%+ of total body weight. It is one of the most effective weight loss medications ever developed.

#### [How is tirzepatide different from semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy)?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1766006195776-a9a0f5a8-f6af)

Both are in the GLP-1 class, but tirzepatide activates an additional receptor (GIP) that semaglutide does not. This dual-action mechanism has shown superior weight loss results in head-to-head clinical comparisons. Many patients who plateaued on semaglutide have found renewed progress with tirzepatide.

#### [What is phentermine and who is it best for?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672840367888-d0042a51-cb6d)

Phentermine is an appetite suppressant that has been used safely for decades. It works by stimulating the central nervous system to reduce hunger. It is best suited for patients who need strong short-to-medium term appetite control and want a more affordable, proven option. TRT Nation providers will assess your health history to confirm it’s right for you.

#### [How much weight can I expect to lose?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672840548785-2a98a754-2415)

Results vary by individual, but patients on tirzepatide in clinical studies lost an average of 15–22% of their body weight over approximately 72 weeks. Phentermine patients typically see meaningful results in the first 12 weeks. Your provider will set realistic, personalized expectations based on your starting point and goals. [Source](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35658024/)

#### [Are there side effects I should know about?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672840551047-5f096be1-9c98)

Tirzepatide’s most common side effects are nausea, mild GI discomfort, and decreased appetite — most of which improve as your body adjusts. At TRT Nation, we compound every tirzepatide prescription with vitamin B12 to make treatment more tolerable and effective. B12 not only helps reduce nausea but also supports energy, metabolism, red blood cell health, and nervous system function—giving you an added boost on your weight loss journey.

Phentermine can cause increased heart rate or mild nervousness in some patients. TRT Nation providers start patients at conservative doses and titrate slowly to minimize side effects.

#### [Do I have to follow a strict diet while on these medications?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1766006203366-55de0829-483a)

No strict diet is required, but our providers offer nutritional guidance to help you maximize your results. The medications significantly reduce appetite naturally, making it much easier to make better food choices without feeling deprived.

#### [Does the cost go up if my dose increases?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672840688125-45f1e5e8-4452)

At TRT Nation, we prioritize transparency and accessibility so you can focus on your health, not unexpected price increases. That’s why we offer tirzepatide at a consistent rate of $219 per month, regardless of dosage.

Unlike some clinics that advertise low introductory pricing only to increase costs as treatment progresses, our pricing remains straightforward and predictable. Our goal is for there to be clarity during the weight loss journey that allows our patients to commit to their health journey without financial surprises along the way.

#### [How do I get started with a weight loss program at TRT Nation?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1672841209659-ab371453-3ace)

Simply complete our online intake form, consult with a provider, and if appropriate, your prescription is sent to your door. No in-person visits required.

#### [Will I gain the weight back when I stop?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1766006204164-6cdab1ab-8b9b)

Weight regain is possible if lifestyle habits aren’t addressed. That’s why TRT Nation combines medication with provider guidance on sustainable habits. Many patients use these medications as a “reset” that helps them establish new, lasting patterns around food and activity.

#### [Where does my medication come from?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1766006206279-3737a865-4129)

Medications are prescribed by licensed healthcare providers and dispensed through regulated U.S. pharmacies following a medical screening and provider consultation.

#### [How is the medication shipped?](https://trtnation.com/weight-loss-therapy/\#1766006205035-b9037a33-4b1d)

All medications are shipped via FedEx. Patients must download the FedEx mobile app to track packages.

## The questions most patients ask first.

### Is this the same as Wegovy / Ozempic / Zepbound?

Try Ageless dispenses **compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide** — the same active ingredients found in brand-name Wegovy, Ozempic, Mounjaro and Zepbound — from state-licensed U.S. pharmacies. Compounded medications are prepared individually and are not themselves FDA-approved, and may differ from the branded product in formulation, inactive ingredients, or delivery device. Your clinician can explain how compounded therapy compares to the brand-name option for your situation.

### Injection or drops — which should I choose?

**Injection** has the most clinical trial data and produces greater average weight loss. **Tirzepatide drops** are needle-free, daily under-the-tongue, and ideal for travel or needle-averse patients. Your clinician will recommend based on your goals, comfort, and budget.

### How does the discount stack?

**The discount is already applied to every plan** — it’s not a “first-month-only” gimmick. You save $100+/mo automatically vs the original list price (up to 50% off on the yearly plan). On top of that, code **SLIM50** gives you an extra $50 off any order, every order — not just the first month.

### What about side effects?

Most common: **nausea, mild constipation, fatigue** in the first 2-4 weeks as your body adapts — almost always resolves with proper titration. Less common: vomiting, diarrhoea. Rare but serious: pancreatitis, gallbladder issues. Your clinician monitors and adjusts to minimise side effects throughout.

### Will I gain it all back if I stop?

Some weight regain is common after discontinuation — this is true for every weight-loss intervention. Best practice is to taper gradually under clinician guidance, maintain protein intake, keep moving, and stay on a low maintenance dose long-term if needed. **It’s a tool, not a sprint.**

### Will my employer or insurance see this?

No. Try Ageless is fully self-pay — **no insurance is involved** and nothing is reported to your insurance carrier or employer. All packaging is plain — nothing identifies the contents on the outside.

## Frequently asked questions

What’s the difference between semaglutide and tirzepatide?+

**Semaglutide** is a single GLP-1 receptor agonist (the active ingredient in brand-name Wegovy and Ozempic). **Tirzepatide** is a dual GLP-1 + GIP agonist (the active ingredient in brand-name Mounjaro and Zepbound). The dual action of tirzepatide typically produces greater weight loss in clinical trials — 21% body weight loss vs 15% for semaglutide.

How does the SLIM50 discount work?+

The **$100+/mo discount is already built into every plan** — you save automatically vs the original list price, up to 50% off on the yearly plan. Code **SLIM50** stacks on top: an additional $50 off every order, not just your first month. Apply it at checkout.

Are Try Ageless GLP-1s FDA-approved?+

The active ingredients (semaglutide, tirzepatide) are FDA-approved as branded products. Compounded medications dispensed by state-licensed 503A pharmacies **are not themselves FDA-approved**, but are legally prescribed and dispensed within the U.S. under federal compounding regulations. Each batch is independently tested for purity and potency.

How much weight will I lose?+

Average results from clinical trials: **14.9% body weight loss on semaglutide at 68 weeks** (STEP-1), **20.9% on tirzepatide at 72 weeks** (SURMOUNT-1). Real-world results vary based on starting BMI, dose, lifestyle adherence, and how long you stay on therapy.

Are there side effects?+

Most common: **nausea, mild constipation or diarrhoea, fatigue, headache** in weeks 1-4. Almost always resolves as the body adapts. Less common: vomiting, injection-site reactions. Rare but serious: pancreatitis, gallbladder issues. **Boxed warning:** potential medullary thyroid carcinoma risk — not appropriate for those with personal/family history of MTC or MEN2.

Why are the drops cheaper than the injection?+

Tirzepatide oral drops are an emerging format with lower compounding cost than the injection, which we pass on as a lower price. The injection has more clinical trial data and is dosed once-weekly; drops are taken daily under the tongue. Both contain tirzepatide. Your clinician will recommend the right format for you.

Can I stack GLP-1s with TRT or Sermorelin?+

Yes — many of our members are on multiple Try Ageless protocols. GLP-1s pair well with TRT (testosterone preserves lean mass during weight loss) and with Sermorelin (sleep, recovery, body composition support). Same provider can manage all your protocols.

We accept all major credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover), as well as **HSA and FSA cards**. Some plans may also be paid via Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Shop Pay at checkout.

Can I cancel anytime?+

Yes. No long-term contracts, no cancellation fees. Pause your subscription, switch formats, or cancel through your patient portal whenever you need.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Why Ozempic®?+

Lowering A1C is an important part of managing type 2 diabetes. But so is managing your potential risk of major cardiovascular (CV) events if you also have known heart disease. Ozempic®, along with diet and exercise, is proven to improve blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. In adults with type 2 diabetes and known heart disease, Ozempic® reduces the risk of major cardiovascular events such as stroke, heart attack, or death. You may also lose some weight. See [ozempic.com](https://www.ozempic.com/) for further details and safety information.

## Weight loss isn't justabout eating less.

It's about understanding why your body holds on to weight. Whether it's _food noise, hormonal confusion, or weight resistance_ from years of _yo-yo_ dieting — it's common, and typically shows up as:

![The hunger that never shuts off.](https://wellorithm.com/assets/images/home-3/insights-sad-plate.webp)

### The hunger that never shuts off.

You eat, but the hunger doesn't stop. Food runs through your mind all day. Even evening. It's called food noise — and it's biological, not willpower.

- **You just ate** and you're already thinking about the next meal
- **The mental load** of food decisions is exhausting all day long

![Your metabolism turned on you.](https://wellorithm.com/assets/images/home-3/26.webp)

### Your metabolism turned on you.

Pregnancy. Perimenopause. Age. Hormones shift how your body stores fat. What worked at 25 doesn't work the same way now.

- **Postpartum weight** that never came off
- **Slower metabolism**, same habits

![Lose 20. Gain 25 back. Every diet makes it worse.](https://wellorithm.com/assets/images/home-3/27.webp)

### Lose 20. Gain 25 back. Every diet makes it worse.

Sound familiar? It's called weight cycling. Each time you lose and regain, your body adapts — holding on to fat tighter and making the next attempt harder.

- **You've lost and regained** the same 20–30 lbs more than once
- **Each restart is harder** with 'hunger hormone' confusion

![This was never about discipline.](https://wellorithm.com/assets/images/home-3/28.webp)

### This was never about discipline.

Food noise. Hormonal confusion. Weight cycling. These are biological — not personal flaws. GLP-1 medications can now treat them at the source.

- **Feeling like** you should do this alone
- **You've looked into this before.** Something keeps bringing you back.

GLP-1 medications carry serious risks, including risks of thyroid C-cell tumors (which includes thyroid cancer) and medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). Talk to your clinician if you get a lump or swelling in your neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing, or shortness of breath.
